September 1874
Treaty 4 signed at Fort Qu’Appelle; Wapella lies within its territory
CPR main line reaches Wapella; townsite laid out
First Hebridean crofters reach Moosomin; Scottish settlement begins south of Wapella
Post office reportedly opens (single source, unverified)
English settlers arrive in the district; second crofter party comes
Wapella School District No. 11 organized
Heppner family settles northeast of town with Hermann Landau’s backing
Abraham Klenman chooses land beside the Heppners; winters in a dugout
Jewish colony grows; Rabbi Edel Brotman and the Bronfman family arrive
Village has CPR station, Queen’s Hotel, a store, a blacksmith and a few houses
Colony school opens, paid for by the settlers
Edward S. Zinng founds the Wapella Post
Killing frost; colony farmers take their first outside loans. Mundell (Commercial) Hotel built
Wapella incorporated as a town; CPR branch line built through the district
Old Town Hall designed by Hutchinson and Nobles and completed
Harry Klenman buys the colony’s first steam threshing outfit
Population approaches 500 (census: 447)
January 13, 1913
RM of Martin No. 122 incorporated; telephones reach the colony district
Jewish farmers summoned under the Lord’s Day Act; case dismissed
Wapella ball club goes 51–5 and wins 16 tournaments
Late 1920s
Ku Klux Klan chapter No. 94 organized at Wapella
About ten dry years; 1937 rust year and crop failure
Wartime issues of the Wapella Post preserved and digitized
Oil discovered in the region
Black Hawks win South Saskatchewan Intermediate B, then provincial Senior B titles
Country schools close; children bused to town
Last of the Barish land sold; the colony era ends
Wapella-raised Dave Dunn wins the Avco Cup with the Winnipeg Jets
Mingling Memories published for the town’s 75th anniversary
Black Hawks win the provincial Senior D championship
Old Town Hall’s ninety-six years as the town office end
Old Town Hall designated a Municipal Heritage Property
September 2017
Grain elevator sold; its rail switch reconnected to the CPR main line
Census counts 278 residents
